recipes.title: Shimmering Starlight Elixir
recipes.description: The Shimmering Starlight Elixir is a splendid first venture for any apprentice seeking clarity of mind — chilled, luminous, and forgiving of a hesitant hand. Blended smooth and threaded with berries and honeyed cream, it is said to still a racing thought within moments of the first sip. Do take your time measuring; a touch too much honey will simply sweeten the effect rather than spoil it, so there is little to fear here.
recipes.instructions:
Yield: 2 servings | Time: 5 minutes
1. Prepare the Vessel: Combine one cup coconut milk, half a cup fresh blueberries, and one tablespoon honey in your blender. Ensure the blades are clean beforehand, so the mixture stays perfectly clear.
2. The Steady Blend: Blend on high until entirely smooth, about thirty seconds. Breathe evenly as you wait — there is no need to rush a good elixir.
3. The Citrus Bond: Squeeze in the juice of the lemon and pulse gently for five seconds to bind the flavors together.
4. The Pour: Divide the elixir between two chilled glasses, taking care to pour slowly so the color settles evenly.
5. The Final Adornment: Garnish each glass with fresh mint leaves and serve at once, while the clarity is at its peak.
recipes.author: Feldren

recipes.title: Feldren's Molten Ember Broth
recipes.description: This broth crackles pleasantly on the tongue, warming from the inside like a captured ember set gently to simmer. It is a forgiving preparation for a scholar in need of restoration after long hours over old texts. The spice builds slowly rather than sharply, so there is no cause for alarm if your first sip surprises you — simply let it settle before the next.
recipes.instructions:
Yield: 4 servings | Time: 25 minutes
1. Prepare the Base: Finely mince the garlic and the fresh ginger.
2. The Gentle Sweat: Warm them in a four-quart pot over medium heat, stirring, until fragrant, about two minutes. There is no need to hurry this step.
3. The Broth's Introduction: Pour in the vegetable broth and whisk in the turmeric and red pepper flakes.
4. The Steady Simmer: Bring to a gentle simmer and cook uncovered for fifteen minutes, until the broth deepens to a rich amber.
5. The Serving: Ladle into bowls while still warm, and take a moment before the first sip.
recipes.author: Feldren

recipes.title: Moonlit Mushroom Draught
recipes.description: The Moonlit Mushroom Draught is velvety enough to soothe even the most travel-worn scholar, best enjoyed slowly by candlelight. Its flavor deepens as the mushrooms surrender their essence to the pot, and though the name suggests a certain mystique, it requires nothing more than patience and a steady stir.
recipes.instructions:
Yield: 4 servings | Time: 30 minutes
1. The Golden Sauté: Slice the mushrooms and sauté with the minced garlic in a three-quart pot over medium heat until deeply golden, about eight minutes.
2. The Broth's Arrival: Add the vegetable broth and the fresh thyme, then simmer uncovered for ten minutes, allowing the flavors to settle into harmony.
3. The Smoothing: Blend with an immersion blender until silken, then stir in the heavy cream.
4. The Careful Warming: Warm gently over low heat, taking care never to let it reach a boil, or the texture will lose its grace.
5. The Serving: Ladle into bowls and enjoy while the steam still rises.
recipes.author: Feldren

recipes.title: Alchemist's Golden Tonic
recipes.description: This glowing amber tonic is a gentle first experiment in restorative brewing, soothing to a sore throat and a troubled spirit alike. There is very little that can go wrong here — should your tea steep a moment too long, it will simply grow a touch more robust, and that is no failure at all.
recipes.instructions:
Yield: 1 serving | Time: 10 minutes
1. The Steeping: Grate the fresh ginger and steep with the turmeric in one cup of hot water for five minutes.
2. The Straining: Strain the liquid into a clean mug, setting the solids aside.
3. The Sweetening: Stir in the honey until fully dissolved.
4. The Final Bloom: Add the juice of the lemon and a pinch of cinnamon, then sip slowly while warm.
recipes.author: Feldren

recipes.title: Feldren's Frostfire Punch
recipes.description: A punch of contradictions — cool as frost yet warm with spice beneath — this preparation rewards a patient hour of chilling more than any rushed effort at the stove. Introduce each element calmly, and the flavors will bloom into balance on their own.
recipes.instructions:
Yield: 6 servings | Time: 15 minutes plus 1 hour chilling
1. The Base: Combine the cranberry juice with the juice of the orange in a large pitcher.
2. The Spiced Infusion: Grate in the fresh ginger and whisk in the cinnamon and honey until dissolved.
3. The Patient Rest: Cover and chill for at least one hour, allowing the flavors time to meld fully.
4. The Serving: Pour over ice into tall glasses and enjoy at your leisure.
recipes.author: Feldren

recipes.title: Bubbling Cauldron Stew
recipes.description: This stew bubbles and pops most satisfyingly as it simmers, rewarding an hour of patience with a deeply comforting result. It is a fine preparation for a scholar who has spent the day in study and now requires something substantial to restore their strength.
recipes.instructions:
Yield: 6 servings | Time: 1 hour 20 minutes
1. The Searing: Pat the beef stew meat dry and sear in a six-quart pot over medium-high heat until browned on all sides, about eight minutes.
2. The Root Vegetables: Add the carrots and the Yukon gold potatoes, each cut into one-inch pieces.
3. The Broth's Introduction: Pour in the beef broth, stir in the thyme, and bring to a simmer.
4. The Long Simmer: Cover and cook for one hour, stirring occasionally, until the meat is tender and the vegetables yield easily.
5. The Serving: Ladle into bowls while hot, and allow a moment for the aroma to settle before your first taste.
recipes.author: Feldren

recipes.title: Sorcerer's Emerald Brew
recipes.description: A vivid green smoothie rumored to sharpen focus before a long session of study, though truthfully its greatest virtue is simply tasting bright and fresh. This is an excellent recipe for a beginner, as there is little precision required beyond a steady blend.
recipes.instructions:
Yield: 2 servings | Time: 5 minutes
1. The Base: Combine the spinach, avocado, and coconut milk in a blender.
2. The Citrus Note: Squeeze in the juice of the lime and add the honey.
3. The Steady Blend: Blend on high until silky smooth, about thirty seconds, pausing to scrape down the sides as needed.
4. The Serving: Pour into glasses and drink promptly, while the color is at its brightest.
recipes.author: Feldren

recipes.title: Feldren's Crimson Potion
recipes.description: A tart, deep red concoction said to embolden the drinker's courage, though its true strength lies simply in the balance of tart and sweet. A gentle recipe, forgiving of an uneven hand at the shaker.
recipes.instructions:
Yield: 2 servings | Time: 10 minutes
1. The Muddling: Muddle the raspberries in the bottom of a cocktail shaker until crushed.
2. The Combination: Add the cranberry juice, the honey, and the juice of the lime.
3. The Shaking: Shake vigorously for fifteen seconds, then strain into small glasses to remove the seeds.
4. The Serving: Serve well chilled, and savor the first sip slowly.
recipes.author: Feldren

recipes.title: Enchanted Spice Draught
recipes.description: A warmly spiced milk brew that lingers pleasantly on the tongue, this is a gentle recipe suited to a quiet evening of reflection. Introduce the spices with care, and let the milk do the rest of the work.
recipes.instructions:
Yield: 2 servings | Time: 15 minutes
1. The Gentle Warming: Warm the milk in a small saucepan over low heat, stirring occasionally.
2. The Spiced Infusion: Whisk in the cinnamon, cardamom, and grated ginger.
3. The Careful Simmer: Simmer gently for five minutes, keeping the milk just below a boil.
4. The Sweetening: Remove from the heat, stir in the honey until dissolved, and pour into mugs to serve.
recipes.author: Feldren

recipes.title: Feldren's Midnight Brew
recipes.description: A rich, dark chocolate drink favored by those working through the night over old tomes. There is real comfort in its steady preparation — simply warm, whisk, and wait.
recipes.instructions:
Yield: 2 servings | Time: 15 minutes
1. The Warming: Heat the milk in a small saucepan over medium-low heat until steaming.
2. The Cocoa Bond: Whisk in the cocoa powder until fully dissolved and no lumps remain.
3. The Melting: Add the chocolate chips and stir constantly until melted and glossy, about two minutes.
4. The Final Touch: Remove from the heat, stir in the vanilla extract, and pour into mugs to serve steaming hot.
recipes.author: Feldren

recipes.title: Keplin's Second Breakfast Hash
recipes.description: There's nothing better than a big skillet of hash when one breakfast simply isn't enough. This one's a real favorite of mine — crispy potatoes, salty bacon, and eggs cooked just how you like them, all in one pan so there's hardly any washing up after. Don't fuss too much over exact timing; just watch and listen, and you'll know when things are ready.
recipes.instructions:
Yield: 4 servings | Time: 35 minutes
1. Dice up your potatoes and onion, nice and even so they cook at the same pace.
2. Fry the bacon in a big skillet until it's good and crisp, then set it aside on a paper towel to rest.
3. Toss the butter into the same skillet, then add your potatoes and onion. Let them cook low and slow, stirring now and then, until golden and soft all the way through.
4. Crumble the bacon back in and give everything a good toss together.
5. Make a few little wells in the hash, crack your eggs right in, cover the pan, and let them cook until the whites set but the yolks stay soft.
recipes.author: Keplin

recipes.title: Hobbiton Shepherd's Pie
recipes.description: This one's always the star of a Hobbiton gathering — layers of savory beef and vegetables tucked under a blanket of buttery mashed potato. It's a bit of a project, but every step is simple, and the smell alone is worth it.
recipes.instructions:
Yield: 6 servings | Time: 1 hour
1. Heat your oven up nice and hot, around four hundred degrees.
2. Boil your potato chunks in salted water until soft enough to mash easily, then drain and mash them up with the butter until smooth.
3. Brown the ground beef in a big skillet, then toss in your diced carrots and the peas, letting everything mingle together.
4. Spread the beef mixture into a baking dish and spoon the mashed potato right over the top, smoothing it to the edges.
5. Pop it in the oven and bake until the top turns golden and you can see the filling bubbling happily at the edges.
recipes.author: Keplin

recipes.title: Keplin's Honey Butter Biscuits
recipes.description: Flaky, golden biscuits dripping with sweet honey butter — perfect for elevenses, or really any time at all. The trick is a light hand; don't overwork the dough and you'll be rewarded with something wonderfully flaky.
recipes.instructions:
Yield: 10 biscuits | Time: 30 minutes
1. Heat your oven up hot, around four hundred twenty-five degrees.
2. Whisk your flour and baking powder together in a big bowl, then cut in the cold butter with a pastry cutter until it looks like coarse crumbs.
3. Stir in the milk and most of the honey, just enough to bring the dough together — don't overmix, or you'll lose that lovely flakiness.
4. Pat the dough out on a floured board and cut it into rounds, setting them on a lined baking sheet.
5. Bake until golden on top, then brush with the last bit of honey and serve them warm, while they're at their best.
recipes.author: Keplin

recipes.title: Cozy Cottage Chicken Stew
recipes.description: A gentle, hearty stew for chilly evenings by the fire — the kind of meal that makes a house feel like a home. It simmers away mostly on its own, so you've plenty of time to put your feet up while it cooks.
recipes.instructions:
Yield: 6 servings | Time: 50 minutes
1. Cut the chicken into bite-sized chunks and sear it in a big pot until lightly browned all over.
2. Add in your sliced carrots, celery, and potato chunks.
3. Pour in the chicken broth and bring everything up to a gentle simmer.
4. Cover the pot and let it cook away until the vegetables turn tender and the broth thickens up nicely.
5. Ladle into bowls and serve it good and hot, maybe with a bit of bread on the side.
recipes.author: Keplin

recipes.title: Keplin's Apple Cinnamon Crumble
recipes.description: A warm, spiced fruit crumble that smells just like autumn settling in over the Shire. It's an easy one to love — sweet apples under a crumbly, buttery topping.
recipes.instructions:
Yield: 8 servings | Time: 55 minutes
1. Heat your oven up to a nice steady three hundred seventy-five degrees.
2. Peel and slice your apples and toss them with the cinnamon right in the baking dish.
3. In a separate bowl, mix the oats, brown sugar, and softened butter together with your fingers until it's good and crumbly.
4. Sprinkle that topping evenly over the apples.
5. Bake until the top turns golden and you can see the filling bubbling at the edges. Serve it warm, with a bit of cream if you fancy.
recipes.author: Keplin

recipes.title: Fireside Mac and Cheese
recipes.description: Rich, creamy, and endlessly comforting — this is the ultimate hobbit hall favorite. There's a bit of stirring involved, but nothing that can't be done with a happy heart.
recipes.instructions:
Yield: 6 servings | Time: 30 minutes
1. Boil the pasta in a big pot of salted water until just tender, then drain it well.
2. Melt the butter in the same pot, whisk in the flour, and let it cook for a minute, stirring the whole while.
3. Slowly whisk in the milk and let it simmer until it's thick enough to coat the back of a spoon.
4. Take it off the heat and stir in the cheddar until it's melted through and smooth.
5. Fold the pasta back in and serve it right away, while it's still hot and gooey.
recipes.author: Keplin

recipes.title: Keplin's Pumpkin Bread
recipes.description: A moist spiced loaf that fills the whole smial with warmth the moment it goes in the oven. It's a lovely thing to bake on a lazy afternoon, and it keeps well for the days after too.
recipes.instructions:
Yield: 1 loaf (10 slices) | Time: 1 hour 15 minutes
1. Heat your oven to three hundred fifty degrees and grease up a loaf pan.
2. Whisk the pumpkin, sugar, and eggs together in a big bowl until smooth.
3. Fold in the flour, cinnamon, and nutmeg, just until there's no dry flour left to see.
4. Pour the batter into your prepared pan and smooth the top over.
5. Bake until a toothpick comes out clean, then let it cool in the pan a bit before slicing.
recipes.author: Keplin

recipes.title: Hearty Vegetable Barley Soup
recipes.description: A rustic, filling soup that sticks to your ribs after a long day of gardening. It mostly looks after itself once it's on the stove, which suits me just fine.
recipes.instructions:
Yield: 6 servings | Time: 55 minutes
1. Sauté your diced onion, carrots, and celery in a big pot until they soften up nicely.
2. Stir in the barley and vegetable broth and bring it to a boil.
3. Turn the heat down low, cover the pot, and let it simmer away until the barley turns tender.
4. Season it to taste with salt and pepper and ladle it into bowls while it's still steaming.
recipes.author: Keplin

recipes.title: Keplin's Blueberry Pancakes
recipes.description: Fluffy stacks studded with berries, best enjoyed at second breakfast when you've really got the appetite for it. They come together quick, so there's no excuse not to make a proper stack.
recipes.instructions:
Yield: 12 pancakes | Time: 25 minutes
1. Whisk the flour, milk, and eggs together in a big bowl until you've got a smooth batter.
2. Gently fold in the blueberries, taking care not to stir too hard.
3. Heat up a buttered griddle and ladle the batter on, one pancake at a time.
4. Cook until bubbles show up on top and the edges look set, then flip and cook a bit more until golden.
5. Stack them up tall and drizzle on plenty of maple syrup before serving.
recipes.author: Keplin

recipes.title: Sunday Roast Chicken
recipes.description: A golden, herb-roasted chicken fit for the whole extended hobbit family, gathered round the table. It takes a bit of time in the oven, but hardly any fuss from you once it's in.
recipes.instructions:
Yield: 6 servings | Time: 1 hour 40 minutes
1. Heat your oven up to four hundred degrees.
2. Rub the whole chicken all over, including up under the skin, with the softened butter, rosemary, and smashed garlic.
3. Arrange your quartered potatoes around the chicken in a big roasting pan.
4. Roast until a thermometer in the thickest part of the thigh reads one hundred sixty-five degrees and the skin turns a deep golden brown.
5. Let the chicken rest a bit before carving, then serve with the roasted potatoes alongside.
recipes.author: Keplin

recipes.title: Myllarra's Forest Quinoa Salad
recipes.description: Gathered from sun-dappled groves, this bright and hearty salad carries the freshness of a morning walk through green fields. It is a dish best made with unhurried hands, honoring each vegetable as it joins the bowl.
recipes.instructions:
Yield: 4 servings | Time: 25 minutes
1. The Grain's Awakening: Cook the quinoa in a small saucepan as the earth intends, then spread it on a pan to cool and breathe.
2. The Garden's Offering: Dice the cucumber and halve a generous handful of cherry tomatoes.
3. The Gathering: Toss the cooled quinoa together with the cucumber, tomatoes, crumbled feta, and a drizzle of olive oil.
4. The Rest: Let the salad chill a while before serving, or enjoy it as the sun finds it, at room temperature.
recipes.author: Myllarra

recipes.title: Elvenwood Mushroom Risotto
recipes.description: Layered with earthy mushrooms drawn from the deep woods, this risotto rewards patience with a creamy, grounding warmth. Stir slowly, and let the rice tell you when it is ready.
recipes.instructions:
Yield: 4 servings | Time: 40 minutes
1. The Mushroom's Turn: Slice the mushrooms and sauté them in half the butter until deeply golden, then set them gently aside.
2. The Rice's Awakening: Melt the remaining butter and toast the arborio rice until it glistens.
3. The Patient Ladling: Add the warm vegetable broth one ladle at a time, stirring without pause, letting each addition vanish into the rice before offering the next — until the rice grows creamy and tender.
4. The Return: Fold the mushrooms and parmesan back into the pot and serve at once, while the steam still rises like mist off the grove floor.
recipes.author: Myllarra

recipes.title: Myllarra's Sunlit Chickpea Curry
recipes.description: A fragrant curry as warm and golden as elven sunlight through the canopy, gentle enough for any table and bright enough to lift a tired spirit.
recipes.instructions:
Yield: 4 servings | Time: 30 minutes
1. The Onion's Softening: Sauté the diced onion until it turns translucent as morning mist.
2. The Spice's Awakening: Stir in the curry powder and let it bloom fragrant in the warm oil.
3. The Simmer: Add the chickpeas and coconut milk and let the pot simmer gently, uncovered, until it thickens.
4. The Greening: Fold in the spinach and let it wilt just briefly, then serve over rice while warm.
recipes.author: Myllarra

recipes.title: Woven Vine Ratatouille
recipes.description: A colorful medley of garden vegetables, braided together like woven vines beneath the summer sun. Arrange each slice with care, as though laying petals in a garden bed.
recipes.instructions:
Yield: 6 servings | Time: 1 hour 10 minutes
1. Warm the oven to a gentle heat, around three hundred seventy-five degrees.
2. Slice the zucchini, eggplant, bell peppers, and tomatoes into thin, even rounds.
3. Arrange the vegetables in overlapping rows in a baking dish, scattering the minced garlic between the layers like seeds along a furrow.
4. Drizzle with olive oil, season lightly, and cover the dish before setting it in the oven.
5. Let it bake until each vegetable yields softly to a knife's touch, then serve warm or at the gentle temperature of the room.
recipes.author: Myllarra

recipes.title: Myllarra's Silverleaf Salad
recipes.description: A crisp salad of silvery greens, sweet berries, and toasted nuts — simple enough to prepare between one breath and the next, yet lovely enough for any table.
recipes.instructions:
Yield: 4 servings | Time: 10 minutes
1. Place a generous bed of baby spinach in a wide bowl.
2. Scatter the walnuts, the crumbled goat cheese, and the dried cranberries over the greens.
3. Drizzle with balsamic vinegar and a touch of olive oil.
4. Toss gently, honoring the greens rather than bruising them, and serve at once.
recipes.author: Myllarra

recipes.title: Elven Lentil Stew
recipes.description: A nourishing, earthy stew simmered slowly beneath the eaves of the forest, deepening in flavor the longer it is left to its own quiet work.
recipes.instructions:
Yield: 6 servings | Time: 50 minutes
1. Sauté the diced carrots and celery until they soften.
2. Add the lentils, cumin, and vegetable broth, and let the pot come to a boil.
3. Lower the flame and let it simmer, uncovered, until the lentils grow tender and the broth thickens into something hearty.
4. Season to taste and serve warm, with crusty bread alongside if you have it.
recipes.author: Myllarra

recipes.title: Myllarra's Roasted Root Medley
recipes.description: A rustic roast of autumn roots kissed with rosemary and golden oil, born of the harvest and simple to bring to the table.
recipes.instructions:
Yield: 6 servings | Time: 45 minutes
1. Warm the oven to four hundred degrees.
2. Chop the sweet potatoes, carrots, and butternut squash into even chunks, honoring their natural shape where you can.
3. Toss them on a baking sheet with olive oil and sprigs of fresh rosemary.
4. Roast, turning once, until the edges caramelize and the roots yield gently to a fork.
5. Serve warm, straight from the pan.
recipes.author: Myllarra

recipes.title: Whispering Wind Pasta Primavera
recipes.description: A light, herb-flecked pasta tossed with the first vegetables of spring, quick enough to prepare between chores and lovely enough to savor slowly.
recipes.instructions:
Yield: 4 servings | Time: 25 minutes
1. Cook the fettuccine in a large pot of salted boiling water until tender, then drain, setting aside a little of the pasta water.
2. Meanwhile, sauté the sliced zucchini and halved cherry tomatoes in olive oil until just tender.
3. Add the pasta to the skillet with a splash of the reserved water and toss gently to bring everything together.
4. Finish with grated parmesan and serve at once, while the aroma still lingers in the air.
recipes.author: Myllarra

recipes.title: Myllarra's Golden Tofu Stir-fry
recipes.description: Crisp golden tofu tossed with garden vegetables in a glossy sauce — a quick dish that honors the harvest without asking too much time of you.
recipes.instructions:
Yield: 4 servings | Time: 25 minutes
1. Press and cube the tofu, then pan-fry it until golden on every side.
2. Add the broccoli florets and sliced bell pepper, letting them dance in the pan until crisp-tender.
3. Stir in the grated ginger and soy sauce, tossing until everything gleams evenly.
4. Serve hot over rice, while the glaze still glistens.
recipes.author: Myllarra

recipes.title: Elvenhome Squash Soup
recipes.description: A silky, golden soup that tastes of harvest and hearthlight, gentle enough to soothe and simple enough to make on any quiet evening.
recipes.instructions:
Yield: 6 servings | Time: 40 minutes
1. Sauté the diced onion and grated ginger until they soften and turn fragrant.
2. Add the butternut squash and vegetable broth and bring to a boil.
3. Lower the heat and let it simmer until the squash turns soft enough to yield at a touch.
4. Blend until silken smooth, then stir in the coconut milk.
5. Warm gently, without haste, and serve hot.
recipes.author: Myllarra

recipes.title: Ghrolg's Beast Slayer Steak Bites
recipes.description: Meat is strength. Sear hard. Eat fast. No sauce needed. Simple is best.
recipes.instructions:
Yield: 4 servings | Time: 20 minutes
1. Dry meat. Salt hard.
2. Heat oil. Pan smoking.
3. Sear beef. Add garlic. Add rosemary. Two minutes side.
4. Rest five minutes. Eat hot.
recipes.author: Ghrolg

recipes.title: Warband Bacon-Wrapped Chicken
recipes.description: Chicken wrapped in bacon. Fat protects meat. Feeds many mouths. No waste.
recipes.instructions:
Yield: 6 servings | Time: 45 minutes
1. Heat oven. Four hundred.
2. Season chicken. Garlic powder. Pepper.
3. Wrap bacon tight. Pin if needed.
4. Roast. Bacon crisp. Meat done.
5. Rest five minutes. Serve.
recipes.author: Ghrolg

recipes.title: Ghrolg's Roasted Root Feast
recipes.description: Roots survive winter. Fire makes them strong. Eat what earth gives.
recipes.instructions:
Yield: 6 servings | Time: 55 minutes
1. Heat oven. High.
2. Cut roots thick.
3. Oil. Rosemary. Salt. Toss hard.
4. Roast. Turn once. Edges black.
5. Pile on platter. Eat.
recipes.author: Ghrolg

recipes.title: Battle-Ready Egg Scramble
recipes.description: Eggs build muscle. Fast food for hard morning. No time waste.
recipes.instructions:
Yield: 4 servings | Time: 20 minutes
1. Cook bacon crisp. Crumble.
2. Whisk eggs. Pour pan.
3. Scramble slow. Add spinach. Add bacon.
4. Top avocado. Eat now.
recipes.author: Ghrolg

recipes.title: Ghrolg's Ironclad Pork Chops
recipes.description: Chop is armor. Sear until hard crust. Inside stays strong.
recipes.instructions:
Yield: 4 servings | Time: 20 minutes
1. Rub chops. Paprika. Garlic.
2. Heat oil. Pan hot.
3. Sear chops. Four minutes side.
4. Rest five minutes. Eat.
recipes.author: Ghrolg

recipes.title: Orcish Almond-Crusted Salmon
recipes.description: Fish wears armor of nut. Crust protects flesh. Strong meal, light work.
recipes.instructions:
Yield: 4 servings | Time: 25 minutes
1. Heat oven. Four hundred.
2. Crush almonds. Mix garlic.
3. Press onto fish.
4. Bake. Crust golden. Fish flakes.
5. Squeeze lemon. Eat.
recipes.author: Ghrolg

recipes.title: Ghrolg's Bonebroth Stew
recipes.description: Long fight needs long broth. Bones give strength. Wait is worth it.
recipes.instructions:
Yield: 6 servings | Time: 1 hour 45 minutes
1. Sear meat. Pot hot.
2. Add broth. Add carrots. Add celery.
3. Simmer long. Ninety minutes.
4. Broth thick. Meat soft. Serve hot.
recipes.author: Ghrolg

recipes.title: Rampage Chicken Drumsticks
recipes.description: Tear with hands. No fork needed. Sticky. Spicy. Good for battle feast.
recipes.instructions:
Yield: 4 servings | Time: 45 minutes
1. Heat oven. Four hundred.
2. Mix garlic. Cayenne. Honey.
3. Coat drumsticks.
4. Roast. Turn once. Deep brown.
5. Eat hot. Fingers sticky.
recipes.author: Ghrolg

recipes.title: Ghrolg's Coconut Curry Beast
recipes.description: Fire in the pot. Chicken tames it. Eat before it cools.
recipes.instructions:
Yield: 4 servings | Time: 30 minutes
1. Cube chicken. Sear hot.
2. Add curry powder. Add ginger.
3. Pour coconut milk. Simmer.
4. Chicken done. Sauce thick. Serve.
recipes.author: Ghrolg

recipes.title: Warlord's Skillet Hash
recipes.description: Fast meal. Between battles. One pan. No waste.
recipes.instructions:
Yield: 4 servings | Time: 30 minutes
1. Parboil sweet potato.
2. Brown beef. Add onion. Add pepper.
3. Add potato. Crisp edges.
4. Serve from pan. Eat.
recipes.author: Ghrolg
